surprises: ⛔ /cma's 'DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE ProtectedRoute' DOES NOT ACHIEVE WHAT ITS COMMENT SAYS, AND THE SCENARIO IT NAMES IS THE ONE D7 IS BUILDING. App.tsx:425-430 says the /cma -> /philosophy redirect is deliberately outside ProtectedRoute because 'advisors bookmark pages and links live in email, so a dead URL is a support ticket for no benefit' and 'gating it would bounce a partner-firm user with a /cma bookmark to /market instead of forwarding them'. MEASURED: /cma sits in the INNER Routes block, which renders only inside DashboardLayout, whose ONLY render site (App.tsx:583, verified -- exactly 1) is <ProtectedRoute><DashboardLayout/></ProtectedRoute>. So the outer guard runs isPathAllowedForFirm(firmId, '/cma') BEFORE the inner redirect is ever matched; /cma is in 0 of 4 allowlists and is not in FIRM_EXEMPT_PATHS (which holds only /change-password), so a partner-firm user IS bounced to /market -- exactly the outcome the comment was written to prevent. BOUND: this is a CODE-plane reading of the router's structure; I did NOT exercise it in a browser, so it is a claim about the code path, not an observed bounce. It bears directly on E-0: the very case the comment reasons about -- a link that lives in email -- is the case that fails.

MY FIRST RECTANGLE WAS FLAT AND WOULD HAVE PUBLISHED A FALSE SECURITY CLAIM: it labelled /dev/page-surface-control 'NONE (public)' because the route carries no inner ProtectedRoute wrapper. The router is nested and it inherits the outer one. Caught by verifying the single row that would become a security claim before reporting it -- not by the parse, which was self-consistent and wrong.
